- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.7) and forecast is flat or rising slowly, model tends to under-forecast sharp upward moves; correct by adding 2–5% to early forecast peaks.
- When sentiment is negative (e.g., <0.3) and forecast is rising, model often over-optimistically extrapolates; correct by reducing forecast slope by 10–20% in early days.
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >10% from prior day), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; apply a “cool-down” rule: reduce forecast by 1–3% per day after peak.
- If sentiment is volatile or mixed (e.g., alternating +/–0.3), model tends to smooth out extremes; correct by allowing 1–2% asymmetric deviation from mean in direction of sentiment.
- Model often underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon; if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative, add 1–3% to forecast mid-range to account for downward correction.
- When sentiment is high and price is rising, model may ignore upcoming policy or supply shocks; adjust forecast downward 1–2% if sentiment >0.8 and price >85.00.
